identity.title: A Clean Slate for Offline Reinforcement Learning

problem.claim: The paper addresses ambiguous offline-RL definitions, entangled designs, opaque implementations, and evaluation practices that hinder fair method comparison.

gap.claim: Prior methods often used extensive undocumented online tuning, while differing boilerplate obscured core algorithmic contributions.

contributions.claim: A taxonomy and transparent protocol that explicitly quantifies online tuning budgets.
Clean single-file implementations and Unifloral, a unified algorithm spanning diverse prior approaches within one hyperparameter space.
Two algorithms developed using Unifloral and the protocol: model-free TD3-AWR and model-based MoBRAC.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state the introduction of Unifloral and the development of TD3-AWR and MoBRAC as new contributions, alongside their taxonomy, protocol, and streamlined implementations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the streamlined implementations achieve substantial speed-ups.
The authors report that TD3-AWR and MoBRAC substantially outperform established baselines under their protocol.
The authors report publicly releasing the implementation.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper identifies ambiguous definitions and entangled designs as causes of inconsistent implementations, weak ablations, and unfair evaluations.
It highlights undocumented online hyperparameter tuning and boilerplate differences as barriers to comparison and attribution.
It introduces a taxonomy, tuning-budget-aware protocol, and minimal single-file implementations.
It proposes Unifloral, then uses it with the protocol to develop TD3-AWR and MoBRAC, which the authors report outperforming established baselines.
The implementation is reported as publicly available.

source_observation.claim: The paper links fair comparison to explicit online-tuning budgets and separates core algorithmic code from boilerplate through minimal implementations.

lessons.interpretation: Making evaluation overhead and implementation boundaries visible can improve the interpretability of comparisons.
lessons.application: When presenting a benchmark, report online tuning budgets explicitly and isolate the method-specific logic in a minimal reference implementation.
lessons.exception: This may be unsuitable when production integration, complex infrastructure, or online adaptation is itself the object of study.

unknowns: No quantitative speed-up figures, baseline identities, task coverage, or tuning-budget values are given.

The abstract specifies that the evaluation protocol quantifies online tuning budgets, but does not give the detailed protocol, statistical treatment, or conditions underlying the reported performance gains.
